requiredFindings.finding: Build scripts are roots of a separate kind, but only paths from production roots make a file production; the final otherwise case makes remaining files test targets. Thus build.rs and its ordinary modules can receive a test exemption, including the platform build script whose exact environment reads the baseline deliberately records. Cargo also permits an explicit build path other than build.rs.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Treat build-script roots and their reachable ordinary code as production for both structural policies (or give them a separate non-exempt class subject to the same restrictions). Discover the effective manifest build target, including custom paths and build=false, as well as default build.rs. Keep the exact reviewed build-script environment baseline. Add a custom build-root/helper control with a planted forbidden spawn and an extra environment read, both refused.

requiredFindings.finding: The plan supports all/any/not but defines exemptions by a path containing cfg(test) or a test-only feature. Presence of an atom is not a test-only guard: cfg(not(test)) is production and cfg(any(test, not(feature = "crash-matrix"))) is reachable with both test and crash-matrix false. Unknown-cfg fallback does not repair these fully parsed expressions. The new graph must not reproduce filename exemptions as syntactic gate exemptions.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Define classification over the Boolean path condition: grant a test exemption only when reachability implies test, and a test-only-feature exemption only when every non-test reachable configuration requires an exact release-refused feature. A satisfiable path with test=false and no such feature is production; uncertain analysis remains non-exempt. Include the enclosing item and inline-module conditions. Add positive all(test, ...) controls and negative not(test), any(test, not(feature = ...)), and mixed test/production paths, for both owner tools with synchronized census data.

rulings.Q9: ACCEPT: keep launcherExec empty until the accepted D1b launcher review supplies its exact production path/function/pattern. D5 tests the schema with synthetic rows only; D1b owns the production exception and combined checks.
